questions.q:
Match the catalysts to the correct process.
&
& Catalyst & Process
A. $TiC{l}_{3}$ i. Wacker process
B. $PdC{l}_{2}$ ii. Ziegler − Natta polymerisation
C. $CuC{l}_{2}$ iii. Contact process`
D. ${V}_{2}{O}_{5}$ iv. Deacon’s process
options: $A \to iii, B \to i, C \to ii, D \to iv$
$A \to iii, B \to ii, C \to iv, D \to i$
$A \to ii, B \to i, C \to iv, D \to iii$
$A \to ii, B \to iii, C \to iv, D \to i$
questions.solution:
The Wacker process is originally referred to the oxidation of ethylene to acetaldehyde by oxygen in water, where the catalyst is tetrachloropalladate$( II )$.

In the contact process, Platinum used to be the catalyst for this reaction, however, as it is susceptible to react with arsenic impurities in the sulphur feedstock, the preferred catalyst today is vanadium $( V )$ oxide $( {V}_{2}{O}_{5} )$.

In the Deacon's process, the reaction takes place at about $400to{450}^{o}C$ in the presence of a variety of catalysts, which include& copper chloride $( {CuCl}_{2} )$.

In Ziegler-Natta polymerisation,& homogenous catalysts, usually based on complexes of $Ti, ZrorHf$,& are used. They are usually used in combination with different catalysts.

questions.q: What is the correct order of spin only magnetic moment (in BM) of $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}, \mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\mathrmV^{2+}$ ?
questions.solution:
Spin only magnetic moments depend upon the number of unpaired electrons, more the number of unpaired electron, greater will be the spin only magnetic moment. ${ }_{25} \mathrm{Mn}=1 s^2, 2 s^2 2 p^6, 3 s^2 3 p^6 3 d^5, 4 s^2\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}=1 s^2, 2 s^2 2 p^6 3 s^2 3 p^6 3 d^5, 4 s^0$

Number of unpaired electrons $=4{ }_{23} \mathrm{ V}=1 s^2, 2 s^2 2 p^6, 3 s^2 3 p^6 3 d^3, 4 s^2\mathrmV^{2+}=1 s^2, 2 s^2 2 p^6, 3 s^2 3 p^6 3 d^3, 4 s^0$
Number of unpaired electrons $=3$ So, the correct order of spin only magnetic moment is $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+} > \mathrm{Cr}^{2+} > \mathrmV^{2+}$

options: more energy difference between $5 f$ and $6 d$ orbitals than between $4 f$ and $5 \mathrm{ d}$ orbitals

greater reactive nature of the actinoids than the lanthanoids

In actinides, both $4 f$ and $5 f$ orbitals are present. These orbitals poorly shields the nuclear charge due to which the energy difference between the $5 f$ and the $6 d$ orbitals will be very low due to which the actinides will show a large number of oxidation states.
Caution
The elements in which the extra electron enters 5 - orbitals of $(n-2)^{\text{th }}$ shell (5f-block elements, actinides) shows the maximum oxidation state i.e. +7.

Identify the correct statements from the following :
I. The ionic radius of \($\mathrm{Pr}^{3+}, \mathrm{Dy}^{3+}$\) and \($\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}$\) follow the order, \($\mathrm{Sm}^{3+}  \gt  \mathrm{Pr}^{3+}  \gt  \mathrm{Dy}^{3+}$\).

(i) The ionic radius of lanthanoids follow the following relation:
Ionic radius \(\propto \frac{1}{\text{ atomic number }}Atomic number \((Z)\) for $\(\mathrm{Pr}=59\)

\end{aligned}\)
Thus, statement (i) is not correct.
(ii) Element Eu \((Z=63)\) can exist in \((+) 2\) and \((+) 3\) oxidation state.
\(\therefore(+)\) 3oxidation state is the most common oxidation state for lanthanoids.
Thus, (+) 2oxidation state oxides oxidises to (+) 3 easily and \(\mathrm{Eu}^{2+} can act as strong reducing agent.
Hence, the statement (II) is correct.
(iii) The electronic configuation for
\(\text{(Pu), }(Z=94)=5 f⁶ 6 d⁰ 7 s²\)
Therefore, it can use maximum of \(6+2=8\) electrons.
Thus, can show +7 oxidation state.
Thus, statement (III) is also correct.
Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation number of $\mathrm{Cr}$ in $\mathrm{CrO}_{5}$ which has the following structure, is
questions.solution:
The structure of $\mathrm{CrO}_{5}$ is a butterfly structure where the central chromium atom is bonded to one oxygen atom via a double bond and to four oxygen atoms via two peroxo linkages.

In the peroxo linkage, the oxidation state of each oxygen atom is $-1$.

Let the oxidation number of $\mathrm{Cr}$ be $x$. The molecule contains one oxo group (O^{2-}$) and two peroxo groups (O_{2}^{2-}$).

The sum of oxidation states in a neutral molecule is zero:

$x + 1(-2) + 2(-2) = 0$

$x - 2 - 4 = 0$

$x = +6$

Answer: $+6$

Addition of aqueous $\mathrm{NaCl}$ to the blue solution gives a white precipitate $\mathrm{O}$. Addition of aqueous $\mathrm{NH}_3$ dissolves $\mathrm{O}$ and gives an intense blue solution.Question: The metal $\operatorname{rod} M$ is
questions.solution: Appearance of blue colour on addition of the metal rod $M$ to the solution of $N$ is an indication that metal may be $\mathrm{Cu}$. Later formation of white precipitate on addition of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and dissolution of this precipitate in aqueous ammonia confirm that while preipitate is of $\mathrm{AgCl}$. This implies that the solution $N$ is of $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$. This confirm that the metal $M$ is only $\mathrm{Cu}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The basic character of the transition metal monoxides follows the order:
(Atomic nos. $\mathrm{Ti}=22, \mathrm{ V}=23, \mathrm{Cr}=24, \mathrm{Fe}=26$ )
questions.solution:
As we move from left side to right side in the first transition series atomic number of elements increases and no. of electrons also increases. Size of elements on moving left to right decreases because effective nuclear charge of nucleus on the outermost shell electron increases. It means electronegativity of atoms increases from left to right, then the power of donation of electrons decreases which means the basicity of that element decreases.
Caution
Students get confused on the order of size of elements in the series, because order of size of elements is not regular in the periods and groups. In periods of increasing atomic number size decreases and on the groups with the increase of atomic number size also increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
In dilute aqueous ${H}_{2}\text{S}{\text{O}_{4}$ , the complex diaquodioxalatoferrate(II) is oxidized by $Mn{O}_{4}^{-}$

For this reaction, the ratio of the rate of change of $\left[H^{+}\right]$ to the rate of change of $\left[Mn{O}_{4}^{-}\right]$ is
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the oxidation of the complex is as given below

$\text{Mn}{\text{O}_{4}^{-} + 5 [ \text{Fe}\left({H}_{2}O\right){\left({C}_{2}{O}_{4}{)}_{2}\right]}^{2 -} + \text{8}{\text{H}^{+} \to 5{\left[\text{Fe}\left({H}_{2}O\right){\left({C}_{2}{O}_{4}\right)}_{2}\right]}^{-} + \text{M}{\text{n}^{2 +} + \text{4}{\text{H}_{2}O$

Hence $- \dfrac{d}{dt} \left[Mn{O}_{4}^{-}\right] = - \dfrac{1}{8}\dfrac{d}{dt}\left[H^{+}\right]$

$\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dt}\left[H^{+}\right]}{\dfrac{d}{dt} \left[Mn{O}_{4}^{-}\right]}$ =$8$

Rate of change of $\left[H^{+}\right]$ is 8 times the rate of change of $\left[Mn{O}_{4}^{-}\right]$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify all the correct statements for Lanthanide contraction.
(A) The covalent properties of the Lanthanide metal hydroxides increases from $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$.
(B) The chemical reactivity decreases from $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$.
(C) $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3$
(D) Zr and Hf have about the same radius.
(E) Separation of Lanthanides from one another is easy
questions.solution: The change in ionic radii is Lanthanide series is very small, their chemical properties are small. Thus, the separation of Lanthanide is difficult due to consequence of Lanthanide contraction. The ionic radii of same positive charge of $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$ decreases. So, the polarizing power towards hydroxyl group increases. Therefore the covalent character increases. Thus, $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3$. $\mathrm{Zr}$ and $\mathrm{Hf}$ have the almost same radius as the electrons in the elements after $\mathrm{Zr}$ are added into the deep seated $4 \mathrm{f}$ orbitals which do not take part in the chemical reaction.
